title: Feasibility of Setting Up a Judicial Service Commission for Judicial Officers
what_it_is: Feasibility of Setting Up a Judicial Service Commission for Judicial Officers

sections.label: Trust in Singapore legal system
sections.summary: A 2020 MinLaw survey found 90% of respondents trusted Singapore's legal system, and Singapore ranked first of 180 countries in the 2021 Heritage Foundation Index.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In a MinLaw Public Perception Survey conducted in 2020, 90% of respondents indicated that they had trust and confidence in Singapore's legal system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Singapore was also ranked overall first out of 180 countries in the Heritage Foundation Index of Economic Freedom 2021 and was given a score of 90.8 for judicial effectiveness.

sections.label: Separate Judicial Service Commission proposal
sections.summary: A separate JSC with its own secretariat, set up under the Constitution and vested with appointment, control and human resource powers, could better nurture specialist judicial officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: A separate JSC with its own secretariat set up under the Constitution and vested with the power of appointment, control and human resource development of the judicial officers in the Singapore Legal Service will be in a better position to nurture a specialist corps of judicial officers.

sections.label: Court of Appeal five-judge benches
sections.summary: Between 2017 and 2020, the Court of Appeal sat as a special five-judge bench about 45 times for novel and complex legal issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Between 2017 and 2020, based on my manual count, the Court of Appeal, the highest Court of our land, has sat as a special five-judge bench about 45 times to deal with novel and complex issues of law.

sections.label: Growth in officer numbers
sections.summary: The number has increased 18 times to over 800 officers, of which 30% are judicial officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Today, this has increased 18 times to over 800 officers, of which, 30% are judicial officers.

sections.label: Feasibility study and specialist tracks
sections.summary: The speaker seeks a feasibility study on the proposal, noting the 2014 shift to specialisation through Specialist Career Tracks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Instead, all I seek to do is to make a case for this Government to agree to conduct a feasibility study on my proposal and revert to this House in due course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The most significant change in recent times was in 2014 when there was a significant shift towards increasing specialisation through the introduction of Specialist Career Tracks.

sections.label: Service policies and officer movement
sections.summary: Each service can set its own performance management, recruitment and training policies, and the speaker says officer movement between Judiciary, AGC and Ministries should continue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Each service can develop its own policies on performance management, recruitment and training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I wish to share my humble view that if a Judicial Service Commission were to be established, movement of officers between the Judiciary, the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) and the various Ministries should continue to be allowed in some form.

sections.label: Movement across branches valuable
sections.summary: The speaker found movement across branches valuable for a rounded view of Singapore's justice system and says such movements should continue if a JSC is established.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I found this movement across branches to be very valuable in providing a more rounded and more informed view of the justice system in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, if a JSC is to be established, such movements should continue to be allowed in some form.

sections.label: IPS survey on court trust
sections.summary: A March Institute of Policy Studies survey found 82% of respondents had a great deal or quite a lot of trust in the Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In a recent survey by the Institute of Policy Studies in March this year, 82% of the respondents had either a great deal or quite a lot of trust in our Courts.

sections.label: Dedicated JSC for HR development
sections.summary: Frequent rotation of Legal Officers under the LSC may limit depth of skills, so the speaker submits it is timely to consider a dedicated JSC for Judiciary officers' human resource development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But having too frequent rotation of Legal Officers under the LSC may not allow them to develop greater depth of skills and expertise required in today's circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Hence, I submit that it is timely that we consider the need for a dedicated JSC to take over the human resource development functions of officers in the Judiciary.

sections.label: Review committee for JSC composition
sections.summary: If the Government proceeds with the proposed review, the speaker suggests a review committee to ensure the new JSC and LSC composition stays robust, especially on HR and personnel management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: If the Government is minded to move ahead with this proposed review, I would suggest that the Government set up a review committee to ensure that the composition of the new JSC and LSC remains robust and responsive to the new challenges ahead, especially in terms of HR and the personnel management framework for the legal officers.

sections.label: Separate Legal and Judicial tracks
sections.summary: In 2014 a significant shift was made: the integrated model was retained but separate Legal and Judicial career tracks were introduced for LSOs in the middle ranks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In 2014, as some Members might know, we made a significant shift.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Although the integrated model was retained, separate “Legal” and “Judicial” career tracks were introduced for LSOs in the middle ranks.

sections.label: LSOs below Grade 2 share
sections.summary: Today, LSOs below LSO Grade 2 constitute about 94% of LSOs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Today, LSOs below LSO Grade 2 constitute about 94% of LSOs.

sections.label: Legal Service restructuring consideration
sections.summary: The Government is prepared to consider restructuring the Legal Service and has set up a Working Group to study arising issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Having heard their perspectives and feedback, the Government is prepared to consider a restructuring of the Legal Service, along the lines I referenced above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We have set up a Working Group to study some of the issues that arise, should any such restructuring proceed.

sections.label: Government to consider Working Group findings
sections.summary: The Government will consider the Working Group's findings and make a further announcement in due course.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Government will consider the findings of the Working Group and will make a further announcement in due course.
